scenes.narration: At 2:46 in the morning, my landline rang. I do not have a landline.
The ringing came from inside the hallway wall. An old, trembling ring, like a bell under water.
I pressed my ear to the wallpaper. It was warm. The ringing was right under my cheek.
It stopped after eight rings. Silence. Then my mobile lit up. Missed call. Home.
Home. The contact I have never saved. I called back. The wall began to ring again.
Someone picked up. Only breathing. Slow. Steady. And the faint hum of a fridge. My fridge.
I walked into the kitchen. The wall by the fridge was warm too. The breathing was in my phone, and in the room.
A voice whispered. Mine. Do not answer this number again. I already did.
The call ended. My phone showed the duration. Four years, three months, twelve days. And a new missed call. Calling from inside.
So tell me. Do you answer, or unplug it?
